steps.say: Loopkind helps neighbors swap help without needing every pair to trade directly. Here, Mara mends clothes and wants plant care, Theo does plant care and wants spreadsheet help, and Jules does spreadsheets and wants mending. Nobody can trade one to one, but together they make a circle. These three are fictional.
Each person lists one thing they offer, one thing they need, how long their session lasts, and when they are free. Now I press Find circles.

The app found one circle of three, and a schedule that fits. Each person gives once and receives once. The timeline shows who meets whom, and no one is booked at the same time twice. Mara has said she will only mend after she receives plant help, and the schedule respects that.

This schedule comes from plain code, not a model. A separate verifier re-checks every session against everyone's availability. Nothing counts until each person reviews the exact plan. I will simulate Jules approving.
Now Theo, then Mara. These approvals are simulated in this demo, and no invitations are sent. If anyone changes a detail, the approvals reset.
Typing a profile by hand is slow, so there is a second way in. Further down, I write a plain note for Mara, the way she might say it to a neighbor.

type: I can mend clothing for 45 minutes. I need plant care. On 2026-10-31 I am free from 09:00 to 11:00 at UTC-07:00. I will start mending only after I receive the plant help. My sewing kit is ready.

steps.say: I press Suggest fields. The server sends this note to NVIDIA Nemotron, a Super model, on Nebius Token Factory. The browser never sees the key. The model must answer in a fixed structure, with an exact quote from my note for every value it fills in.
Here is the live answer from Nemotron: the offer, the need, forty-five minutes, the free window, the receive-first condition, and the materials, each with its quote.

The app checks this before showing it. A value whose quote is not in the note, a duration the quote does not state, or a time outside the chosen date is rejected. Unknown facts stay blank. The draft is applied as unreviewed, so Mara still has to confirm it.

Loopkind uses the model to read language, and uses its own code to decide what is feasible and what is allowed. That is how a neighborhood can trade help in a circle, with everyone agreeing to the plan.
